newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Public Bank picks HK dollars.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Public Bank picks HK dollars.

text.p: Public Bank brought a rare Malaysian issue to Hong Kong dollar debt markets on Monday.

The three-year HK$1.0 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue was launched at par to float at 25 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return is 32 basis points to top-tier participants.
Chase Manhattan Asia, HSBC Markets, Standard Chartered Bank, Sanwa International Finance and Tokyo-Mitsubishi International are the arrangers.
Proceeds of the issue, which was launched through the bank's head office, will be used for general working capital, one of the arrangers said.
The borrower has not applied to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for use as collateral at the HKMA's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
Even without LAF status, bankers were generally positive on the deal because of the rarity of Malaysian paper, particularly Hong Kong dollar paper.
Malaysian credits have become increasingly popular as issuance from other investment-grade countries, namely South Korea and Thailand, continues to be sparse.
Public Bank is rated A2 by Moody's Investors Service.
Bankers have been expressing interest in the Public Bank deal since rumours of its existence began circulating a few weeks ago.
"Even before the deal launched, a lot of banks called to register their interest," remarked one of the arrangers.
Still, some bankers complained that without the benefit of LAF the issue was a bit tightly priced.
In other news, bankers said Hong Kong's International Bank of Asia has mandated six banks to arrange a HK$1.0 billion three-year non-LAF FRCD issue.
The mandated arrangers are Bayerische Landesbank, Fuji International Finance Hong Kong, Sakura Finance Asia, Standard Chartered Bank, WestLB Hong Kong and Westpac Banking Corp.
Hong Kong Building and Loan Agency launched a HK$1.0 billion loan facility into general syndication today, arranger Schroders Asia said.
The three-year loan pays an interest margin of 150 basis points over HIBOR. Fees range from 25 to 52.5 basis points.
The deal is secured over residential mortgages in Hong Kong.

Merrill Lynch announced today that SM Investment's floating rate note issue was increased to US$110 million from US$100 million. SM Investments is the parent company of Philippine shopping mall developer SM Prime.

Pakistan began roadshows for its upcoming FRN issue today in Singapore. The country plans to tap capital markets further in its July/June fiscal year and is considering Samurai bonds, a Ministry of Finance official told Reuters.
